chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated from Hammad ibn Uthman from Isma'il al-Ju'fi who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say:
The grandfather shares the inheritance with the siblings, even if they were one hundred thousand.

key_terms.الْإِخْوَةَ: The siblings (brothers and sisters of the deceased)
key_terms.الْجَدُّ: The grandfather (specifically paternal in this context)
key_terms.مِائَةَ أَلْفٍ: One hundred thousand (used to indicate a large, indefinite number)
key_terms.يُقَاسِمُ: Shares the inheritance (takes a portion alongside others)

ai.seo_question: Does the grandfather exclude siblings from inheritance in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* establishes the principle of *qismah* (equal division) for the paternal grandfather when competing with siblings, a ruling that distinguishes him from the father who typically excludes siblings. Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to resolve juristic debates regarding whether the grandfather acts as a *hajib* (excluder) or a *nasib* (shareholder), affirming that he shares equally with any number of siblings. This ruling is foundational in Shia inheritance law (*'ilm al-fara'id*) for determining the distribution of the residual estate after fixed shares are allocated.
